title: Economy of Minds: Agents That Bid to Act
hook: Skip the orchestrator. Let agents bid in auctions for the right to act, pay each other, and accumulate wealth — and collective intelligence emerges from the market, not from central control.
key_points: Hayek-inspired: agents compete in auctions for the right to act, exchange payments, accumulate wealth.
Economic signals induce decentralized credit assignment — planning with no global orchestrator or comms protocol.
Effective agents grow wealthy and are mutated (exploit); bankrupt ones are replaced (explore).
Starting from weak agents, the economy yields emergent multi-step reasoning beating monolithic baselines on 5 tasks.
content_html: How can a population of agents organize itself into stronger collective intelligence without anyone in charge? Qi and colleagues borrow Friedrich Hayek's theory of decentralized market coordination and build an agent economy: agents compete in auctions for the right to act, exchange payments, and accumulate wealth from environmental rewards. Those simple economic signals turn out to induce decentralized credit assignment — agents end up planning without any global orchestrator or explicit communication protocol.
extra_html: The population evolves by economic selection. Agents that prove effective accumulate wealth and are mutated via exploitation; ineffective ones go bankrupt and get replaced via exploration. Starting from weak agents, the economy produces emergent multi-step reasoning strategies and, the authors report, outperforms stronger monolithic baselines across five agentic tasks spanning mathematical reasoning, financial research, scientific research, accelerator design, and distributed-system optimization. The paper also offers theory linking local incentives to long-term global performance. The provocation: rather than engineering coordination by hand, design the right decentralized incentives and let coordination emerge. See the arXiv link for the full results.

flashcards.prompt: How do agents in Economy of Minds get 'selected' over time?
flashcards.back_html: Through economic selection: effective agents accumulate wealth and are mutated via exploitation, while ineffective ones go bankrupt and are replaced via exploration.

flashcards.prompt: What role do the economic signals (auctions, payments, wealth) play in the system?

choices.text: They induce decentralized credit assignment, driving planning without global orchestration
They are a logging layer that doesn't affect agent behavior
They require a central controller to clear every auction

flashcards.explanation_html: The economic signals themselves drive decentralized credit assignment and planning — no central orchestrator or explicit communication protocol needed.
